name: PandaDoc
subcategory: PDF editing, document workflows and electronic signatures
tagline: Create reusable proposals and a low-stakes signature workflow from templates

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 60 documents/year (shown as 5/month), 2 recipients/document, 5 templates, unlimited seats, storage and fillable fields

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: Unlimited document uploads/eSignatures; up to 5 templates; 14-day no-card trial

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Starter plus CRM integrations, branding/content library, up to 3 deal rooms, approvals; some web forms, bulk send and automations are optional

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Per-seat or per-document quote; CPQ, workflow automation, SSO, unlimited team workspaces, optional notary/API

pricing.freeTierCaps: 60 documents/year (5/month), 2 recipients per document, 5 templates, unlimited users, storage and fillable fields
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (Starter $35 or $19/user/month; Business $65 or $49/user/month); 14-day trial; Enterprise quote
pricing.hiddenCosts: Over-limit documents: $3.50 Starter monthly, $2 Starter annual, $2.60 Business monthly; unused documents do not roll over; external automations cost $39/month per account on Business; taxes excluded

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For PandaDoc, create reusable proposals and a low-stakes signature workflow from templates. The hard boundary is document crm, payments, analytics, integrations, signature evidence, and sales workflow, plus document fidelity, identity, and compliance.
coreLoopDIY: Create reusable proposals from templates, run a low-stakes signature workflow, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store.
whatYouLose: document CRM, payments, analytics, integrations, signature evidence, and sales workflow
replacementScope: personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow
ongoingBurden: format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for PandaDoc because the visible editor is reproducible, but reliable rendering and legally defensible signature workflows are not a casual side project. The recurring cost buys format edge cases, fonts, rendering, encryption, signatures, evidence, retention, storage, backups, and legal requirements, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Stirling PDF
priorArt.desc: Active open-source web application for a broad set of PDF operations.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Build reusable proposals and quotes from products and saved lines, generate PDFs, email them, and collect online approval or signatures; heavier than PandaDoc because it is also an ERP.

rejectedAlternatives.name: DocuSeal
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Excellent once a document already exists, but it does not replace PandaDoc's proposal authoring, pricing tables, and content-library workflow.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal document tool or low-stakes signature flow DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for PandaDoc in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Python 3.12, FastAPI, pikepdf, LibreOffice headless, and PostgreSQL; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: create reusable proposals from templates, run a low-stakes signature workflow, preserve originals, generate auditable outputs, and keep files in a user-owned store.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Keep every original immutable and write each operation to a versioned output file.
Support merge, split, reorder, rotate, compress, watermark, redact, OCR, and Office-to-PDF conversion.
Render page previews and warn when fonts, forms, signatures, or encryption may be altered.
For signature mode, place fields, invite signers, record consent, and seal a final PDF hash.
Maintain an append-only event log with timestamps, document hashes, and delivery outcomes.
Add file expiry, download, deletion, backup, and a prominent low-stakes-use warning.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out qualified or regulated electronic signatures.
Deliberately leave out government identity verification.
Deliberately leave out full Acrobat-level editing and enterprise document governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
